transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jonah Reed (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (NovusBank Head of Platform), Mark Davids (NovusBank Security Architect), Priya Singh (NovusBank Compliance), Tom Wu (NovusBank SRE)
Links shared: security_deck_v2.pdf (redwood.com/s/secure-deck), audit-log-sample.csv (sandbox link), soc2-type2-redwood.pdf

---
00:00 Lena Ortiz: okay we can start, yep thanks everyone for joining, we wanted to cover the security checklist items for the POC this week and make sure the SSO test is scheduled.
00:12 Morgan Ellis: great thanks lena, appreciate it. quick agenda recap: SSO/SAML status, audit logs + retention, SOC2 artifacts, and any outstanding compliance asks. priya from my team will run through the audit logs demo.
00:26 Priya Patel: hey all, hi, quick note we pushed the sandbox changes last night so you should have log export and retention toggles available under the admin console link i shared. there may be a small permissions glitch depending on your idp metadata.
00:45 Mark Davids: when you say retention toggles, is that at the tenant level or per-route? we need to control both application data and token logs separately for compliance.
00:58 Priya Patel: good question, currently we support three tiers: ephemeral (30 days), standard (90 days), and extended (7 years) - the current pilot default is standard 90 days. per-route retention is on the roadmap but we have route labels you can use to approximate segmentation.
01:18 Tom Wu: 7 years seems heavy, for pilot we probably want 90 days but need to capture what fields are retained. is pii stripped from the logs?
01:29 Priya Patel: audit logs contain request metadata: timestamp, route, model, token-count metrics, requester id (redacted if configured), and an optional request snapshot. pii stripping: we offer masking rules and an auto-redact option; it's not foolproof for arbitrary json, we'll need to test with your sample payloads.
01:50 Priya Singh: for compliance we need to show evidence of masking and retention configs. also, ensure the audit logs include admin actions for who changed a config.
02:03 Morgan Ellis: yep we can include admin action events - change, create, delete of policies - and tie them to SSO user ids. that depends on SSO binding working correctly so the ids map.
02:20 Lena Ortiz: can you recap SSO status? last week you said there was a small metadata mismatch.
02:27 Priya Patel: right, we imported your IdP metadata but there was a certificate thumbprint mismatch. i tried a manual override but we need your SRE to push the corrected metadata or we can do an on-call swap. tom?
02:42 Tom Wu: i can push the updated metadata today, just need the exact fields. i'll send the metadata to priya after this call.
02:49 Priya Patel: perfect, once we have the corrected metadata i'll run the SAML assertion test and show the nameid mapping. we'll also demonstrate attribute mapping for groups -> roles to validate RBAC.
03:05 Mark Davids: about RBAC, we can't have open admin rights for everyone on your console. does redwood support custom roles and scoping to projects?
03:15 Priya Patel: yes we have RBAC with custom roles and project scoping. for the pilot we'd recommend two roles: developer (invoke models, view logs) and admin (manage policies, export). we can pre-create roles for your test accounts.
03:32 Morgan Ellis: i'll coordinate with lena on who should get admin for pilot; we normally advise limiting admins to security and platform engineers.
03:40 Lena Ortiz: agreed. next, SOC2: you said you'd share the report?
03:45 Morgan Ellis: yes SOC2 Type II -- i'll share the control matrix and the report PDF after the call. note that some details are redacted in the public report but we can provide a more detailed bridge letter if needed under an NDA.
03:58 Priya Singh: the scope matters: does SOC2 cover the dedicated/dedicated-pool product you provisioned for the POC or only hosted api? we need clarity on which deployments are in-scope.
04:12 Morgan Ellis: good point. the SOC2 covers Redwood hosted control plane and the hosted inference environment; for Dedicated and Private deployments we have separate attestations or can provide architecture diagrams + controls evidence. for the POC you're on a dedicated pilot pool but still using our managed control plane -- i'll mark that explicitly in the artifacts i send.
04:36 Mark Davids: can you confirm encryption at rest KMS handling? who holds the keys in the pilot?
04:44 Priya Patel: by default keys are managed by Redwood KMS, but for Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys via your cloud KMS or HSM. for this pilot we can switch to your KMS if you prefer; it requires a brief key-sync and permissions setup.
05:05 Tom Wu: we will likely want CMK (customer-managed keys) for the PII flows. what's the timeline to enable that in sandbox?
05:13 Priya Patel: usually 3-5 business days to validate access, create key policies, and test decryption flows. we can fast-track if you provide IAM contacts and permissions today.
05:25 Lena Ortiz: ok we'll try to provide those contacts.
05:28 Jonah Reed: i just want to call out that for the evaluation we'll also capture perf telemetry; if we roll to dedicated we'll do in-region key policies too.
05:40 Mark Davids: another ask: audit log integrity, do you provide immutability or log shipping to our SIEM?
05:49 Priya Patel: yes we support streaming audit logs to customer endpoints: s3, kafka, or syslog. for immutability we recommend shipping to an append-only S3 bucket with object lock enabled on your side. we also provide signed digests of daily logs for tamper-evidence.
06:10 Tom Wu: shipping to our SIEM (internal splunk) would be ideal; can the pipeline include redaction before shipping? we don't want raw prompts leaving our network if possible.
06:22 Priya Patel: redaction can be applied pre-shipment. there's a transform lambda that strips configured fields and masks patterns before sending. we can demo the pipeline in the sandbox.
06:36 Lena Ortiz: please demo that, it's high priority.
06:39 Priya Patel: noted. next item: data residency — are you expecting EU-only storage for any of the pilot data?
06:48 Lena Ortiz: for a subset yes, some accounts are EU customers and we must keep logs and outputs in eu-west-1. can redwood support region pinning at the tenant level?
06:59 Priya Patel: yes tenant-level region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we have region controls but not strict legal residence guarantees. for this pilot (dedicated pool in us-west) we can create a eu region tenant mirror if you want to test cross-region behavior.
07:21 Mark Davids: ok we'll note that as a requirement for scope.
07:25 Morgan Ellis: next, on telemetry: what alerts do you want? we can generate security alerts for policy changes, failed SSO assertions, unusual token volumes, or large export requests.
07:37 Mark Davids: policy change auditable with email to security and a slack integration would be great. also anomalous usage detection to catch exfil patterns.
07:46 Priya Patel: we have built-in anomaly scoring on token volumes per user; we can emit alerts to slack or pagerduty. the anomaly model is tuned for typical app patterns, for banking flows you may want to increase sensitivity.
08:02 Tom Wu: sensitivity tuning is fine. pair that with immediate lockout for repeated failed SSO assertions?
08:12 Priya Patel: yes we can set automatic lockouts on the IdP side or disable sessions after n failures. we'll show the config options in the demo.
08:21 Lena Ortiz: wrapping towards next steps — timeline wise we want SSO validated, audit logs shipping, and retention masks tested by next week's call. is that realistic?
08:31 Morgan Ellis: yes that is realistic if we get IdP metadata and IAM contacts today. action owners we laid out earlier.
08:38 Priya Singh: one question on legal: for pilot data are you taking any rights over model outputs? our legal asked about data usage/retention in your terms — does Redwood use customer prompts for model training?
08:51 Morgan Ellis: quick answer: by default redwood does not use customer prompts to train public models; we have an opt-in program for improving model quality that customers must consent to. all customer data by default is isolated and covered by our DPA. i'll share the DPA excerpt with the call notes.
09:09 Mark Davids: good. can you also share the list of endpoints that will be accessible from our VPC? network allowlist etc.
09:18 Priya Patel: yes network details and allowlist ips are in the security deck i'll send — we also support VPC peering for Dedicated.
09:26 Tom Wu: about the audit log CSV you shared, i noticed some fields look scrambled — maybe transcription or mapping issue. can you confirm column mapping?
09:34 Priya Patel: sure i think the sample was auto-exported, i'll attach a mapping doc. the csv fields: event_time, user_id, action, resource, route, model, token_count, request_snapshot. mapping doc will show redaction rules.
09:51 Lena Ortiz: for the SSO test, can we do a joint test next week on wednesday? 2025-09-17 at 10am PT?
09:58 Morgan Ellis: yes i'll book that, setting a calendar hold now and will send invite after the call.
10:04 Jonah Reed: i'll also kick off a pilot health dashboard for you so you can see progress metrics during the week.
10:12 Priya Patel: demo plan for next call: live SAML assertion, audit log export and redaction pipeline, and a quick CMK key-swap test if you provide IAM contacts.
10:25 Mark Davids: perfect. any blockers from our side other than providing metadata and IAM contacts?
10:31 Lena Ortiz: none on my side. we'll follow up with priya the idp xml and tom will give the iam contacts.
10:38 Morgan Ellis: great thanks everyone. recap of commitments: i share SOC2 + security deck and dpa excerpt by friday; priya runs the sandbox demos and shares steps; tom provides idp metadata & iam contacts; we schedule sso test 2025-09-17.
10:56 Priya Singh: thanks all, appreciate concise notes.
11:02 Morgan Ellis: thanks team, we'll send notes and mark items in the jira - meeting end.
